title: Atlassian security policy, API key and audit log changes
volume: None on a normal day. Admins change security policies and create admin API keys a few times a year; audit log exports come with audits.
mdr_note: These detections are yours to work. Sophos MDR doesn't work custom detections, and a case your own case rule opens from them is Managed By Self.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: Three custom detection rules for the Atlassian organization audit log, on the CloudAudit records the library's Atlassian parsers write. They make a detection when an admin changes a security policy, creates an admin API key, or exports the audit log. Each rule matches sensor type Atlassian only.
notes:
Setup:
- Add the library's Atlassian parsers and the example bridge in bridges/atlassian-org-audit, and run the bridge with an organization API key that has the read:events:admin scope, as the parser entry says. Then run the check-your-data search to see events arrive.
- The organization audit log needs Atlassian Guard or a Cloud Enterprise plan.

How it works:
- Atlassian doesn't publish its action keys, so the rules read the names the bridge takes from the event actions list: the action's group, Security policies, which the parsers write as the event type, and its display name, which they keep in additional_event_data.
- The API key and export rules take the display names Created admin API key and Exported organization audit log, from Atlassian's audit log activities list.

Testing:
- In a lab tenant on 2026-11-23, each query returned exactly the sample lines tests.json lists in Data Lake Search, and the rules run offline on the same 7 records agreed. The samples went in with their dates moved to the day before the test, so they fell inside the search's time range.
- As live rules there, each one fired on exactly its sample lines within about a minute. The lines went in 23 minutes after the rules were made, and every rule fired on the first send.
- No Sophos detector made a detection on the lines these rules take.
- The events went in through bridges/atlassian-org-audit, run once on the lab machine against a local mock of the Atlassian Organizations REST API that served the sample events, and posted to HTTP Ingest as gzipped NDJSON, the way the bridge's README says.

Known gaps:
- The bridge polls, so detections arrive up to one poll interval after the event.
- If Atlassian renames an activity, the rule that names it stops matching; run the check-your-data search for the display names you see.
